clue.text: Dick insured, lacking Ken's arrangement with this ancient order

indicators.note: lacking says the letters of the second group are taken away from the pool of the first
arrangement says the letters that remain are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Dick has taken out insurance, without Ken's arrangement, in some ancient fraternity.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of DICK INSURED, strike out K, E, N and S (the letters of KEN'S), and rearrange the remaining seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celtic priesthood of ancient Gaul and Britain was the order of druids, and anything belonging to it is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Remove carbon from French solid fuel

parts.note: de is French for from
coke is a solid fuel made from coal

explanation.surface: Instructions to strip carbon from French coal.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean the carbon deposits out of an engine is an old motoring verb.

clue.text: Free one soul in torment

indicators.note: a soul in torment is in turmoil, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Release a single tortured spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to unfasten or let go.

clue.text: Ephesian silversmith of unusual 'merit in classic divinity

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: deus is Latin, the classical language, for god

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the following word are made strange by rearranging

explanation.surface: A craftsman of remarkable merit in classical religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns MERIT into METRI, which goes 'in' DEUS. In Acts 19 Demetrius, a silversmith making shrines of Diana, stirs a riot in Ephesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names the maker of silver shrines at Ephesus who opposed Paul.

clue.text: Feature nothing on one's lake in oriental art style

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
nothing is the figure O
one's gives the Roman numeral I plus S
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A face with nothing on it beside a lake, in an eastern art style.
explanation.definitionFit: The European decorative fashion imitating Chinese motifs is a style of art.

clue.text: Receptacle for Iago's purse?

parts.note: In Othello, Iago says 'Who steals my purse steals trash', so his purse is rubbish and needs a bin for refuse

explanation.surface: Asks where Shakespeare's villain keeps his money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare line 'Who steals my purse steals trash' (Othello) turns the purse into trash, so its proper container is the household rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A household bin collects trash, which Iago says his purse is.

clue.text: John Peel's colourful beginning

parts.note: the hunting song about John Peel opens with the words '... ken', and colourful points to a word for a colouring agent

explanation.surface: A huntsman's song has a vivid opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The folk song begins 'D'ye ken John Peel'; the colouring agent sounds and looks like its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or colouring agent shares its letters with the song's opening contraction of 'do you'.

clue.text: To enjoy winter, sport learners need to acquire this

definitions.text: To enjoy winter, sport learners need to acquire this

parts.note: to enjoy winter sport is to ski
L is the learner's plate, doubled for the plural as in LL

explanation.surface: Novices who want to enjoy the snow must learn the technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'winter' is surface punctuation. Read whole, the clue also defines: beginners must acquire this.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners must gain expertise, the ability to do a thing well, before they enjoy the slopes.

clue.text: Where the woman for Holmes threatened to cause a scandal

definitions.text: Where the woman for Holmes threatened to cause a scandal

parts.words: Where the woman for Holmes threatened to cause a scandal
parts.note: Irene Adler, always called the woman by Sherlock Holmes, is the adventuress of the Conan Doyle story set around a royal scandal in a central European kingdom

explanation.surface: Asks where Holmes's favourite adversary nearly caused a royal scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Conan Doyle's 'A Scandal in Bohemia' has Irene Adler, to Holmes always 'the woman', threatening the King of Bohemia with a compromising photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conan Doyle story's title names the kingdom, a region now in the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Scandinavians: and not Kentish types

parts.note: nor means and not
Kent is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
men are types, fellows

explanation.surface: Northerners, as opposed to people from Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings and other old peoples of the north were Scandinavians.

clue.text: Flower-girl, daughter of Jaques's old man

definitions.text: girl, daughter of Jaques's old man

explanation.surface: A flower seller who is the daughter of a character's father from As You Like It.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's 'seven ages' speech in As You Like It calls the sixth age 'the lean and slipper'd pantaloon'; in the harlequinade the girl is the daughter of Pantaloon.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a garden flower also called aquilegia, and the pantomime sweetheart of Harlequin is the old man Pantaloon's daughter.

clue.text: Some Olympic horses in circulation on Olympus

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Horses at the ancient Games being passed around among the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympic horses' looks like the subject, but 'Some' takes part of those letters; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the ethereal fluid that flowed in the veins of the gods instead of blood bears this name.

clue.text: Nothing is heard in the north of this scourge

indicators.note: is heard says a word is spoken, and in the north says it is spoken in a northern English way

parts.note: in northern English dialect nothing is nowt

explanation.surface: Not a sound is reported from up north about a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWT is the northern English word for nothing; said aloud it matches the Russian whip, whose K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian whip once used to flog criminals is a scourge, an instrument for punishment.

clue.text: Standard French — or Middle English if Lamentations are included

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Lam is the abbreviation for the Book of Lamentations in the Bible

explanation.surface: A flag in French, or the old English language if a book of the Bible is added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are included' puts the if-plus-Lamentations piece inside Middle English. 'Standard French' reads as the French language but means the French royal banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred red banner of the early French kings is a standard in the sense of a flag.

clue.text: This means an adequate income for the unemployed.

definitions.text: This means an adequate income for the unemployed.

parts.words: This means an adequate income for the unemployed.
parts.note: a person of private means needs no job, so this word joined to means describes one living without employment on their own income

explanation.surface: A definition of what unemployment benefit should provide.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'This means' as 'This ... means': the phrase 'of ___ means' is a private income large enough that no work is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of private means is self-supporting, needing no employer.

clue.text: Dickens of a job, his, opposing a would-be Simon Templar in court

definitions.text: Dickens of a job, his, opposing a would-be Simon Templar in court

parts.words: Dickens of a job, his, opposing a would-be Simon Templar in court
parts.note: a dickens is a devil, Simon Templar is the fictional hero known as The Saint, and the papal court once named an official to argue against making a candidate a saint

explanation.surface: A lawyer with the tough task of opposing a fictional adventurer in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' means the devil (as in 'what the dickens'); Simon Templar is the hero of Leslie Charteris's novels, called The Saint, so a would-be Simon Templar is a candidate for sainthood.
explanation.definitionFit: In canonisation the Church appointed an official to argue against a candidate's case, and today the phrase means anyone who argues a contrary view.

clue.text: Poor goop Harry's description of mountains

indicators.note: poor says the letters are in a bad state, so they are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive 's gives no letter

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow named Harry writes about mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of physical geography deals with the relief and formation of mountains.

clue.text: Noisy bird, exclamation mark!

explanation.surface: A shrieking bird, with emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The South American screamers are loud waterbirds; printers once called the exclamation mark by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is named for its loud cry, and the punctuation mark shouts out its sentence.

clue.text: Fear of confinement in hospital, our cab having crashed

indicators.note: a taxi that has crashed is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient laid up in hospital after a taxi smash is frightened of enclosed spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes all of HOSPITAL and OUR CAB; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phobia is a dread of being shut in small or enclosed spaces.

clue.text: Is a cat one variety of Siamese for example?

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take another order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cat is one breed of Siamese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siamese' looks like the cat breed; it is a person from Siam, an Asian.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam lies in Asia, so its people and things are Asian by origin.

clue.text: Devout return to Westminster church in town

indicators.note: return says the letters of the word for devout are turned back

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, devout
Westminster's London postcode is SW1, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A pious person goes back to a Westminster church in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns PI into IP. Ipswich is the county town of Suffolk, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk port is a town in East Anglia.

clue.text: "The very houses seem —" (Wordsworth)

parts.note: the gap completes a line of Wordsworth's sonnet Composed upon Westminster Bridge, describing London at dawn

explanation.surface: A line of poetry about London with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's sonnet on Westminster Bridge reads 'Dear God! the very houses seem asleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the sonnet the dawn city's houses seem to be sleeping, at rest.

clue.text: One of refined taste, Marius?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man called Marius is a person of discerning palate.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Pater's novel is titled 'Marius the Epicurean'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet devoted to refined pleasure follows Epicurus, and Pater's hero Marius is given that title.

clue.text: Disconcerted the crowd at university

parts.note: up means at university, as in going up to Oxford
a set is a crowd or group

explanation.surface: Unsettled by the people at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disturbed or thrown off balance is ruffled.

clue.text: What Cynara's lover flung riotously with the throng

definitions.text: What Cynara's lover flung riotously with the throng

parts.words: What Cynara's lover flung riotously with the throng
parts.note: Ernest Dowson's poem to Cynara has the speaker say he flung flowers riotously with the throng

explanation.surface: Asks what a poet's lover threw about with the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The line from Dowson's 'Non sum qualis eram' (Cynara) runs 'I flung roses, roses riotously with the throng'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flowers flung in Dowson's line are the thorny garden blooms named there.

clue.text: Scholar takes this, dropping one school subject

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar by degree

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let fall from the word before it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A student takes a certain class and drops another subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes I (one) from THIS to give THS.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic and geometry lessons taught in British schools go by this short name.

clue.text: Swank at little cost in a way in London

parts.note: something at little cost is cheap
side is old slang for swank, putting on airs

explanation.surface: Showing off cheaply on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swank' (in old slang, 'putting on side') comes first in the clue but last in the answer. Cheapside is a historic street in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The old market street in the City of London is a thoroughfare, and a way is a road.

clue.text: An officer's pass

explanation.surface: An officer's permit.
explanation.walkthrough: Col is the abbreviation for Colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: Col abbreviates Colonel, an army officer, and a col is a mountain pass between peaks.

clue.text: A detailed account when genuine carries copyright with it

indicators.note: carries says the word for genuine holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: genuine means real
C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled symbol
taken as written

explanation.surface: A true story with copyright protection attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A recounting of facts in order is an account that sets out the details.

clue.text: Trifles before the dance can help to cure Jack's dullness

definitions.text: can help to cure Jack's dullness

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: toys are trifles, things of small value
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Small things before a dance might cure a boy's boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy': a shop selling playthings would cure that.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop of playthings supplies play, the proverb's cure for a dull boy.
